sections.h2: What is the quickest way to sell a LaGrange house?
sections.html:
Most LaGrange owners choose between three routes: an agent listing, a sale by owner, or an as-is cash offer. Pick by looking at repair needs, your deadline and the net you want. LaGrange serves as the seat of Troup County, roughly 60 miles southwest of Atlanta where the Piedmont foothills begin, and the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 34,730 residents against 30,858 in the 2020 count.

Prices run well below metro Atlanta suburbs, so do not borrow a Cobb or Gwinnett number for your plan. Start from local figures and a frank look at the house.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about LaGrange housing?
sections.html:
Renters make up a large share of the city. For 2020 to 2024 the Census Bureau shows just 39.7 percent of homes occupied by their owners, a median home value of $216,300 and a median gross rent of $1,073. In a place where most households rent, a landlord or investor is a likely buyer.

  • Households: 12,993 at 2.41 people each
  • Median household income: $43,708 (in 2024 dollars)
  • Land area: 42.14 square miles, around 732 residents per square mile
  • Average trip to work: 22.0 minutes

With 60.3 percent of homes not owner occupied, a house that needs work suits a buyer who plans to rent it out. The poverty rate is listed at 22.9 percent, so monthly cost weighs heavily for local buyers.

sections.h2: What shaped LaGrange and where does the work come from?
sections.html:
The city was incorporated in December 1828 and takes its name from a French country estate owned by the Marquis de Lafayette's wife, which he said resembled this landscape during an 1825 tour. In the late 1800s it grew as a railroad and textile town, and as mill work moved overseas the economy shifted toward a mix of manufacturing and distribution.

Interface, a carpet tile manufacturer, was founded in LaGrange in 1973 and has its largest manufacturing center here. A Walmart distribution center sits in the area, and in November 2021 Remington Arms announced it would move its global headquarters to LaGrange with 865 planned jobs over five years. LaGrange College, the oldest private college in Georgia, and Point University and West Georgia Technical College add education jobs. The city is also a full-service utility provider, covering electricity, natural gas, water, sewer and refuse, so a sale means transferring or closing city utility accounts.

Local landmarks include the 1939 Troup County Courthouse, listed on the National Register of Historic Places, and Bellevue, an 1850s house that is a National Historic Landmark. In 2000 LaGrange was named Intelligent Community of the Year, and the city has offered free internet service to every household since.

sections.h2: How do roads and schools affect selling a LaGrange home?
sections.html:
Buyers who commute care about access, and LaGrange has it: Interstates 85 and 185, U.S. 27 and 29, and Georgia 219 and 109 all pass through. West Point Lake, a few miles west, draws bass fishermen and water sports fans.

The Troup County School System covers LaGrange, Hogansville and West Point. The system runs 11 elementary schools, middle schools named Callaway, Gardner Newman and Long Cane, and Callaway, LaGrange and Troup County high schools. Private options include LaGrange Academy, Lafayette Christian and Hillside Montessori. Name the school zone in your listing, but tell buyers to confirm zoning with the district.

sections.h2: What did the 2023 tornado change for LaGrange sellers?
sections.html:
An EF2 tornado hit the southern half of LaGrange on January 12, 2023 and injured four people. If your house was in or near that path, buyers will likely ask about roof work, fallen trees and any claims filed afterward.

  • Keep contractor invoices and the final inspection records for storm repairs.
  • Request a claims history from your insurer if a buyer asks for it.
  • Photograph any repaired roofing, windows or siding before you list.

Documented repairs cost far less in negotiation than unexplained patches. Buyers paying cash still want to see receipts.

sections.h2: When do Troup County tax bills come due?
sections.html:
The county's Tax Commissioner lists November 15 as the yearly deadline, with penalties and interest after that. Value is fixed as of January 1 at 40 percent of fair market value, and the tax equals that assessed value times a millage rate set by the school board, the county and any other taxing body.

Troup's Board of Assessors is appointed by the county commissioners but runs on its own. To learn whether a city levy applies to your parcel, call the Tax Commissioner at 706-883-1620.

TopicTroup County's published rule
Yearly payment deadlineNovember 15, after which penalties and interest accrue
Share of market value taxed40 percent
Homestead filing periodJanuary 1 through April 1; no filing means the exemption is waived for that year
Time to contest a value45 days counted from the notice date
Superior Court appeal fee$25.00

Sources: Troup County Tax Commissioner and Troup County Property Appraisal FAQ.

sections.h2: What can a LaGrange owner do about a high assessed value?
sections.html:
File an appeal against the Annual Assessment Notice within 45 days of the notice date; the county says the right is lost after that. Send the assessors sales data or photographs of comparable homes that recently sold. A hearing goes to the Board of Equalization, whose members are chosen by the grand jury and who charge nothing, or to arbitration, where each side pays its own arbitrator and half the cost of a third.

Appeal only if the value looks well above what similar houses bring. The assessment does not set your sale price, but a lower one trims the tax a buyer will carry.

sections.h2: What code rules and permits apply in the City of LaGrange?
sections.html:
The city follows the state's mandatory minimum codes, and effective January 1, 2026 these include the 2024 International Residential Code and Building Code with Georgia amendments. Ask Community Development about any job started under an earlier code year.

Code enforcement sits within the LaGrange police department, and officers deal with overgrown grass and weeds, litter, abandoned or inoperable vehicles, nuisances and sewage problems. The stated goal is voluntary compliance, so on a vacant or inherited house keep the grass cut and the exterior clear. Find out about any open notice before you sign.

sections.h2: How is a LaGrange deed transfer taxed?
sections.html: Georgia's rate is $1 for the first $1,000 or fractional part of $1,000 and 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part of $100 of the price. The contract can shift the payment to the buyer, and recording waits until it is paid.

faqs.q: Would a cash offer suit a LaGrange rental house?
faqs.a: It can, once the tenant situation is clear. Landlords often prefer a quick cash closing on a rental needing work, and with most local homes renter occupied, investors are active. Get lease terms in writing first.

faqs.q: When are Troup County property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 15 each year. The Tax Commissioner says penalties and interest begin after that date, and the office answers questions at 706-883-1620.

faqs.q: How much time do I get to contest a Troup assessment?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the date shown on the Annual Assessment Notice. After that, the right to appeal that year's value is gone.

faqs.q: When is the Troup homestead filing period?
faqs.a: January 1 through April 1. Skipping it waives the exemption for that year, and you must own and live in the home on January 1.

faqs.q: Do I need to close my LaGrange utility accounts when selling?
faqs.a: Yes, arrange it with the city. LaGrange itself supplies electricity, gas, water, sewer and refuse service, so schedule a final reading and move the accounts to the new owner.
